floor_history.headline: Object-model fix (D_800A9CF8 header struct, base+offset evidence) drops honest floor 40 -> 13; loop body byte-exact; residual is pre-loop sched1/local-alloc coupling fully attributed (birthing-leaf re

frontier.hypothesis: An ordinary-C spelling exists in which src's pseudo has two live sets at flow time with the second set becoming a no-op move after allocation (e.g. src derived on both arms of the count check from the same temp), demoting the reload copy from birthing and yielding the target order at 0.
frontier.mechanism: sched.c birthing_insn_p requires reg_n_sets==1; with 2 sets the copy keeps priority 1, the store wins T-2 by potential_hazard, the count load is blocked one cycle after the store and lands before addr/store.
frontier.next_probe: Spell 2-3 such forms, sandbox each, verify in .flow that reg 72 keeps 2 sets and in .sched that insn 20 shows priority (1) at T-2.

frontier.hypothesis: tools/sched_solver on block 0 of form C can enumerate exactly which attribute change (boost removal vs. added block-0 consumer) yields the target order, and tools/ra_solver classify can confirm the local-temp seat, before more spellings are burned.
frontier.mechanism: order-exact scheduler model + local-alloc model on the banked pre-sched chain (dumpsC .combine).
frontier.next_probe: Run the solvers on dumpsC, map the winning vector to C, measure.

frontier.hypothesis: If src's second set cannot be produced, a form where the reload copy has a block-0 consumer other than the store (dst or i derived from the temp) is the last ordinary-C lever; probability low because the target block 0 has no extra insns.
frontier.mechanism: a consumer removes the copy from the T-2 ready list; the consumer must itself be deleted/merged later.
frontier.next_probe: One measurement per shape; kill with the sched trace.
